_comment: Stat values that the generated cards.json gets wrong. Two sources, both better than the community database: values marked as read off a printed card scan in assets/cards/en/, and values taken from the publisher's championship-legal English parts lists (v1.02). Where the two disagree the parts list wins — it is the company's current data, while some scans are older printings (040's scan is watermarked Ver.2019 Crowdfunding). Points can ONLY come from the parts list: the printed card leaves the points box deliberately blank, and rulebook 6.1 says the online list wins. Where the publisher has issued more than one revision the NEWEST wins: GoF is on v1.021, which repriced the faction and redesigned card 180; the other factions are still on v1.02.
_scope: Only stats confirmed wrong against a scan are listed. No systematic sweep of every card has been done, so absence from this file does not mean a stat is correct.
_shape: cards maps a card id to the stat fields to overwrite.

Card 180 is a REDESIGN: PL29 Stealth Chassis became PL29 All-terrain Chassis, losing Silence and gaining a Jump. (This note used to say the text layer cannot be parsed and to read it by rendering the pages. That is true of the plain text layer, which comes out in jumbled reading order, but NOT of the table: pdfplumber's extract_tables() resolves the page into 29 named columns cleanly, and every value it gives agrees with what the rendered reading had already banked - the four ranges, the two Small sizes, both point totals and this whole redesign. Use extract_tables.)

_notes.ZHDR-101: N11 Vanguard I "Scutum". The 1.021 regunning gave the shield drone a gun the community bundle never had: Action B Single Shot, Firing, Auto, 3Y1R, Range 3, Omni-direction Firing and Melee Firing (list row ZHDR-101). Supplying a NEW action needs this file's wholesale `actions` replacement, so the array carries the final _A too - including its list English, which cannot live in action_overrides because applyStats runs after applyActionFixes and would discard it. The _A content is otherwise the bundle's own, zh and jp included; _B is English-only because no 1.021 Chinese exists to copy.
_notes.ZHDR-102: N12 Vanguard II "Crossbow". The 1.021 regunning removed Interception 1 from its action (see action_overrides ZHDR-102_A, which drops the load-bearing inline keyword); this entry removes the CARD-level 拦截X chip that would otherwise keep advertising a rule the drone no longer has. The other two keywords are kept, with the stray bullet the bundle put in front of Omni-direction Firing dropped.
_notes.116: S100 Shield + R6SS SMG (D), the RIGHT-hand discard face. Same gap as 118/120 and found the same way: the UN 1.02 list gives row 116 the Freehand keyword and our card had an empty array, so a Mech that Disarmed this shield offered no free hand. Unlike the Fairy pair this card is RELEASED (UN_CORE). Its action text comes through action_overrides 116_A rather than here, the action already existing.
_notes.118: MDXS "Fairy" System + R6 SMG (L) (D). The bundle gave the two Fairy discard faces NO actions and NO keywords at all, where the publisher's Part Data UN 1.02 EN rows 118 and 120 print the Thruster passive and the Freehand keyword on both. That was a LIVE bug, not a display one: disarm rewrites the equipped card id to the discard face, flightGrant() counts Thruster halves off the equipped cards, and the pair needs two - so a Mech whose Fairy arm was Disarmed lost flight the publisher says it keeps. The action text is copied verbatim from the FRONT face 117_B, which the list's own row 118 matches word for word (typo included, "it's"), so the zh is the printed sibling text rather than a translation. jp is omitted on purpose: the bundle's 119_B jp fields are corrupted (they hold the gun action's text), so nothing unverified is carried over. These entries are the first use of applyStats supplying `actions` - action_overrides.json cannot do this, being keyed by an action id that must already exist.
_notes.120: MDXS "Fairy" System + R6 SMG (R) (D). Mirror of 118: text from front face 119_B, referencing the (L) arm.
_notes.181: PLK400 "Centaur" High-mobility Chassis. THE PDF SUPERSEDES THE SCAN - OTTO's ruling, 2026-08-24: the card scans in our data are old and the publisher's 1.02x parts lists are the current information, so where they disagree the list wins and a clause the list does not carry does not belong. Our reminder line said Push X moves the target "in straight line in the direction this unit is facing, then this unit performs the same movement", and the Chinese agreed (然后本单位执行同样的移动), so the two were consistent with each other and with nothing else: NEITHER the rulebook glossary NOR the publisher's GoF 1.021 Extra Info for this exact row has any follow-up move by the attacker. The engine never implemented one either - offerShove moves only the victim - so the app was already right and the card text was the thing lying. Replaced with the list's block verbatim, which also supplies the Command Coordination reminder we were missing. The Chinese is assembled from our own glossary's zh values for the four keywords, not translated by hand; note that the glossary's 推动X already read 沿任意直线方向 with -1链接值 and no follow-up, agreeing with the list all along.
_notes.179: PL1 Standard Chassis. Description was empty; the list's Extra Info for row 179 is the Command Coordination reminder. Same sourcing as 181.
_notes.182: PL35 Armored Chassis. The card's own reminder line DEFINED THE WRONG KEYWORD: it spelled out Push X, in both languages, on a card whose keyword field is 击退X Knockback X and whose Kick the publisher prints as Knock Back 1. Those are different rules - Push X also takes 1 Link from a target Mech, and a Mech driven to 0 Link Shuts Down - so the page was teaching a cost this card cannot impose. Display-only (knockbackOf reads ACTIONS, never the card body), but it is the half a player actually reads. Replaced with the Extra Info the publisher's GoF 1.021 EN list prints for row 182, which is Knock Back X plus Command Coordination. The Chinese is the glossary's own 击退X value rather than anything invented. Completes the 182_B correction in action_overrides.json.
_notes.180: PL29 All-terrain Chassis. Stripping `keywords` was not enough: the card's own description was still the SILENCE reminder line, in both languages, so the reference printed "· Silence: Optical Camouflage and Low Profile will not be removed" on a card the v1.021 redesign took Silence away from. The keyword chip was gone and the sentence explaining it stayed. Replaced with the Extra Info column the list actually prints for this row, Airborne Movement and Command Coordination. The zh is cleared for the same reason as action 180_B's: the bundle's Chinese is the superseded design, and we do not hold the v1.021 Chinese to put in its place. Display-only, unlike 180_B - maneuverPrintsSilence() reads card.keywords, which the empty array had already fixed.
_notes.093: TM31KC "Gray Wolf" KC Experimental Core. These four cards (093, 095, 539, 545) were the last card-level description fields whose `en` held Chinese: each is a keyword reminder line the community bundle never translated. The reference already suppressed them rather than print Chinese (englishOnly in reference.ts), so nothing was visibly broken, but an `en` field holding Chinese is wrong data and the English was sitting in the publisher's lists all along. This one is the Fire in arc reminder, verbatim from Part Data UN 1.02 EN, row 93 / TM31KC.
_notes.095: TM39B "Viper II" Low Profile Core. The Silence reminder, verbatim from Part Data UN 1.02 EN, row 95 / TM39B.
_notes.539: TM31Q "Wild Cat" Battle Core. The Command Generation X reminder, from Part Data UN 1.02 EN, row 539 / TM31Q. The list prints a full-width colon; written here with an ASCII one, which is what cleanRulesText would produce anyway.
_notes.545: Ls297 Dual Autocannon. The Suppression reminder, from Part Data PD 1.02 EN, serial PDBP-102. That list files the card under QR 555 where ours is 545; the serial and the full name both match, and the reminder text is the generic keyword definition rather than anything card-specific, so the id difference does not bear on it. It matches our 压制 glossary entry word for word.
_notes.078: DTG-30M "Hyena" MG Type. Database says offensive; the printed stance strip reads DEF. All three Hyenas (078, 079, 080) print DEF, and the database only has 080 right.
_notes.079: DTG-30S "Hyena" Missile Type. Same as 078: database offensive, card prints DEF.
_notes.159: AMDS210 "Delphinium" Automatic Defense System. Database says mobility; the printed strip reads OFF · ✗ in red. Its Move box is printed blank, so the recorded Move 0 is correct and is not patched.
_notes.161: ADK15/MAS "Porcupine" Microwave Type. The card database records Move 0, but the scan prints the same ↑5 Move box in the bottom-right as its two siblings ADK15D (160) and ADK15P (543), both of which the database has at 5.
_notes.074: GM-35 Anti-Armor Mine. Recorded as electronic -1; the card prints "--" in the Electronic box, meaning no value. Every other card printing "--" (154, 155, 267, 268, PDAM-003/004/005) is recorded as 0, so -1 is a misparse of the dash. It matters because electronicValue() sums this field, so -1 actively subtracts 1, and the reference page renders it as "E-1".
_notes.158: DBP "Turtle Shell" Barricade. Same "--" misparse as 074.
_notes.ZHAM-002: M60 "Boomerang" Missile. The card prints only two stat boxes, an orange Electronic 1 and a grey Armor 3, with no blue Dodge box at all; the database records armor 0 and dodge 6. Box colours were confirmed by sampling pixels, not by eye: the orange box spans x540-594 and the grey x618-666, and no blue pixels appear anywhere in the stat row. On this same GOF template ZHAM-003 prints orange/blue/grey for electronic/dodge/armor and ZHAM-004 prints blue/grey for dodge/armor, so a lone grey box after the orange one is Armor. Confirmed by a second reader against the card: 1 electronic, 3 grey, no Dodge icon present.
_notes.503: RT-16B "Avalanche" Assault Core. We had 48. Both the community parts sheet and the publisher's championship list say 60, and points are never printed on a card, so there was never a scan that could settle it. This closes a long-standing open question. Source: championship-legal EN parts list v1.02 (publisher).
_notes.040: SPHX-3 Supporting Arm. We had Parry 0. The publisher list gives Armor 4 AND Parry 1; our scan shows only the Armor 4 box and is watermarked "Ver.2019 Crowdfunding", so it predates the current data. Source: championship-legal EN parts list v1.02 (publisher).
